controversies/infant-vs-believers-baptis: Should the children of Christians be baptised, or only those who personally repent and believe?
Implicit from Tertullian’s counsel of delay (c.203), the dispute exploded in Zurich in 1525 and has divided Protestants ever since; the WCC’s Lima document (1982) found convergence but not agreement.

God’s promise is to us and to our children. As Israel’s infants received the covenant sign, so the children of believers receive baptism. Grace comes before our response — none of us chooses God first — and infant baptism proclaims exactly that. The church has done this since the apostles.
No explicit infant baptism in the New Testament.
Faith precedes baptism in every recorded case.

Christ commanded us to make disciples and baptise them. Every baptism in the New Testament follows hearing and believing. The new covenant is written on hearts; its sign belongs to those who know the Lord. Infant baptism created a Christendom of the baptised but unconverted.
Tertullian counsels delay of baptism for little children.
Cyprian’s council: infants need not wait for the eighth day.
Anabaptist kingdom at Münster discredits the movement.
John Smyth’s believers’ baptism in Amsterdam: Baptist beginnings.
Karl Barth criticises infant baptism in The Teaching of the Church Regarding Baptism.
Baptism, Eucharist and Ministry (Lima) records convergence.

Unresolved. Paedobaptist churches comprise the large majority of Christians; credobaptist churches are the largest Protestant family in many countries and dominate Pentecostal and Global South independent Christianity. Mutual recognition agreements usually exclude or carefully qualify the infant/believer question.
Persecution and martyrdom of Anabaptists (16th century).
Birth of Baptist, Mennonite and believers’-church traditions.
Linked to debates on religious liberty and church-state separation.
controversies/baptism-and-salvation/ques: Is baptism the means by which God regenerates and forgives, or an ordinance that testifies to salvation already received by faith?
controversies/baptism-and-salvation/titl: Does baptism save? Regeneration vs ordinance
controversies/baptism-and-salvation/summ: A question dividing sacramental churches (Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Anglican), Restorationists, Reformed and Baptists/evangelicals, and a running debate between Churches of Christ and Baptists in America.
controversies/baptism-and-salvation/side: Scripture says baptism saves, washes away sins and gives new birth. It is not our work but God’s Word with water. To deny this is to turn God’s gift into a mere human pledge and to rob believers of a concrete promise: "I am baptised".

We are saved by grace through faith, not by any rite. Baptism is commanded and precious: it pictures our union with Christ and publicly confesses it. But to say the water saves is to make salvation depend on a ceremony and to unchurch every believer who died unbaptised.
Cornelius received the Spirit before baptism.
Weakens the strong New Testament language about baptism.
Peter said, "Repent and be baptised for the remission of sins." We baptise believers only, and we believe God meets them there with pardon. This is not works but the obedience of faith.
controversies/baptism-and-salvation/time: Zwingli’s Of Baptism reinterprets sacraments as pledges.
Luther’s Small Catechism on what baptism gives.
Trent, Session VII, canons on baptism.
Campbell’s Lunenburg letter on the unimmersed.
controversies/baptism-and-salvation/reso: No agreement. Sacramental churches teach baptismal regeneration; Reformed churches speak of baptism as a means of grace not tied to its moment; Baptists and most evangelicals regard it as an ordinance; Churches of Christ teach baptism for remission.
controversies/baptism-and-salvation/cons: Shapes evangelism (altar call vs baptismal invitation), emergency baptism and funeral practice.
controversies/spirit-baptism-subsequence: Is the baptism in the Holy Spirit a distinct experience after conversion (evidenced by tongues), or what happens to every believer at conversion?
Baptism in the Spirit: second blessing or conversion?
The defining theological question of Pentecostalism, debated with Reformed, Baptist and sacramental traditions since 1901, and within the charismatic movement.

The disciples were believers before Pentecost; the Samaritans believed and were baptised but had not yet received the Spirit; the Ephesian disciples received the Spirit when Paul laid hands on them and they spoke in tongues. Luke shows a pattern of empowerment that every believer may and should seek.

Paul says all believers have been baptised by one Spirit into one body. To have the Spirit is to belong to Christ. The Acts episodes mark the gospel’s advance across new frontiers. Seek to be filled, again and again — but do not divide the church into the baptised and the un-baptised in the Spirit.
Asa Mahan’s The Baptism of the Holy Ghost (Holiness movement).
Agnes Ozman speaks in tongues at Parham’s Bethel Bible School, Topeka.
Assemblies of God defines tongues as initial evidence.
Dunn’s and Bruner’s critiques of subsequence.

Classical Pentecostal churches retain subsequence and initial evidence; many charismatics in historic churches speak of a "release" of the Spirit given in sacramental initiation; Third Wave and most evangelicals hold Spirit baptism at conversion with ongoing fillings.
controversies/jesus-name-new-issue/quest: Must baptism be performed "in the name of Jesus" (Acts 2:38), or in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19)?
controversies/jesus-name-new-issue/title: The "New Issue": Jesus’ name or triune name?
controversies/jesus-name-new-issue/summa: A 1913-1916 controversy within early Pentecostalism that began over the baptismal formula and became a dispute over the Trinity, producing the Oneness Pentecostal movement, which stands outside historic Nicene orthodoxy.
controversies/jesus-name-new-issue/sides: The apostles never once baptised with the triadic words; they baptised in the name of Jesus Christ. Jesus is the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, for in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily. We restore apostolic practice.
"In Jesus’ name" is not a formula.

Jesus himself commanded baptism in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and the church has obeyed from the Didache onward. "In the name of Jesus" describes the authority and character of Christian baptism. The new teaching departs from the faith of the whole church about God.
Acts never records the triadic formula.
controversies/jesus-name-new-issue/timel: Arroyo Seco camp meeting, Los Angeles: R. E. McAlister’s comment on apostolic baptism.
Frank Ewart and Glenn Cook re-baptise each other in Jesus’ name.
Assemblies of God adopts a Trinitarian Statement of Fundamental Truths; Oneness ministers leave.
controversies/jesus-name-new-issue/resol: The Assemblies of God and most Pentecostals affirmed the Trinity; Oneness Pentecostals formed separate bodies (Pentecostal Assemblies of the World, United Pentecostal Church International). Dialogue (e.g. Society for Pentecostal Studies) continues without resolution.
controversies/jesus-name-new-issue/conse: Racially integrated early Oneness bodies (PAW) were later divided along racial lines.
controversies/chalcedon-controversy/ques: After the incarnation, is Christ one person ‘in two natures’ (Chalcedon), ‘one incarnate nature of God the Word’ (Miaphysite), or two natures and two qnome in one parsopa (Church of the East)?
controversies/chalcedon-controversy/summ: The fifth-century Christological struggle divided the churches of the Roman and Persian worlds into three communions that endure today. Each side claimed to defend both Christ's full deity and full humanity; each accused the others of either dividing or confusing them.
controversies/chalcedon-controversy/side: Chalcedonian (Rome, Constantinople, later Protestants)

We confess with Cyril one and the same Son, and with Leo that he is acknowledged in two natures. Unless the humanity remains truly human after the union, Christ is not consubstantial with us and our nature is not healed; unless the person is one, he is not our Saviour but a pair. Our four negatives — without confusion, without change, without division, without separation — fence the mystery from both errors without claiming to explain it.
Leo's Tome: each nature does what is proper to it in communion with the other.
Two natures guarantee real consubstantiality with both God and us.
Cyril himself accepted the Formula of Reunion (433), which spoke of a union of two natures.
‘In two natures’ looks like two subjects (Miaphysite objection).
Insisting on one hypostasis compromises the integrity of each nature (East Syriac objection).
John 1:14
Romans 9:5
Hebrews 2:14–17
Hebrews 4:15
Miaphysite (Oriental Orthodox)

We hold to the faith of Cyril and of Ephesus: one incarnate nature of God the Word. We anathematise Eutyches; Christ's humanity is perfect and unmixed. But after the union we will not count two natures as if two subjects acted side by side — for the one who was born, suffered and rose is God the Word himself. Leo's Tome, which makes each ‘form’ act, revives the very Nestorianism that Ephesus condemned.
‘One incarnate nature of God the Word’ is Cyril's own formula.
Salvation depends on the Word himself being the subject of suffering and death (1 Corinthians 2:8).
Chalcedon reinstated Ibas and Theodoret, sympathisers of Nestorius.
‘One nature’ risks absorbing the humanity (Chalcedonian objection).
Dioscorus had rehabilitated Eutyches in 449.
John 1:14
1 Corinthians 2:8
Hebrews 2:14
Galatians 4:4
East Syriac (Church of the East)

The eternal Word cannot change or die; the man he assumed is complete, with his own concrete reality, growing in wisdom and learning obedience. Two natures and their two qnome are united in one parsopa of the Son, worshipped as one Lord. To say ‘God died’ confuses Creator and creature. We follow Theodore the Interpreter, whose exegesis of the Scriptures is faithful to the Gospels' human Jesus.
It protects divine impassibility and the integrity of Christ's human moral struggle.
Qnoma means concrete nature, not person; two qnome do not imply two sons.
Ephesus (431) was held without the Antiochene bishops present.
A union of two concrete individuals looks like two subjects (Cyrilline objection).
Refusing Theotokos denies that the one born of Mary is God.
Luke 2:52
Hebrews 5:7–9
controversies/chalcedon-controversy/time: Nestorius becomes archbishop of Constantinople and opposes the title Theotokos.
Formula of Reunion between Cyril and John of Antioch.
Second Council of Ephesus restores Eutyches; Leo's Tome is ignored.
Council of Chalcedon defines ‘one person in two natures’.
Emperor Zeno's Henotikon tries to bypass Chalcedon; Acacian schism with Rome (484–519).
Synod of the Church of the East at Seleucia-Ctesiphon adopts dyophysite language.
Pope Paul VI and Pope Shenouda III sign a common Christological declaration.
controversies/chalcedon-controversy/reso: The council resolved it for Rome and Constantinople, but caused lasting schism. Modern dialogue has produced agreed statements recognising a common faith beneath different terms; full communion has not been restored, chiefly over the status of councils after 451 and of saints condemned by the other side.
controversies/chalcedon-controversy/cons: Three enduring Christian families: Chalcedonian, Oriental Orthodox and East Syriac.
Religious alienation in Egypt and Syria that some historians link to the ease of the Arab conquests (debated).
The Church of the East's mission across Asia, and the Ethiopian and Armenian national churches' Miaphysite identity.
